standard_prerequisites.name: A finite module over a Noetherian normal domain is reflexive if and only if it is the intersection of its localisations at height one primes
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the criterion that the proof verifies.

standard_prerequisites.name: The coefficients of the minimal polynomial of an element integral over each height one localisation lie in those localisations
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-minimal-polynomial-normal-domain}, cited at proof lines 5679-5681
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the coefficients lie in every height one localisation.

standard_prerequisites.name: A Noetherian normal domain is the intersection of its localisations at height one primes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1}, cited at proof lines 5681-5683
standard_prerequisites.use: Brings the coefficients back into the domain.

core_obligations: Reduce to showing that the integral closure is the intersection of its height one localisations (proof lines 5672-5674).
Take an element of that intersection and its minimal polynomial over the fraction field (proof lines 5675-5678).
Use the minimal polynomial result to place the coefficients in every height one localisation (proof lines 5679-5681).
Apply the intersection theorem for normal domains to conclude that the element is integral (proof lines 5681-5684).
proof_roadmap: Reflexivity criterion reduces to an intersection (proof lines 5672-5674).
Minimal polynomial of an element of the intersection (proof lines 5675-5681).
Intersection theorem puts the coefficients in the domain (proof lines 5681-5684).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the integral closure of a Noetherian normal domain in a finite field extension is reflexive as a module over the domain, assuming it is finite. The proof uses the criterion that a finite module over a normal domain is reflexive exactly when it is the intersection of its localisations at the height one primes. An element of that intersection is taken, its minimal polynomial over the fraction field is written down, and the cited result that the coefficients of the minimal polynomial of an integral element lie in the localisations at height one primes is applied; the intersection theorem for normal domains then puts those coefficients back into the domain, so the element was integral and lies in the integral closure.
